property_summary: After a non-owner deposits 1 ether, the owner calls sendMoney(address(this), 1 ether, ''); the reference contract sends the ether to itself (no net balance change), while the buggy contract treats the non-owner as the only allowed caller and thus doesn't revert, also sending 1 ether to itself—but the key difference is that after the call, the reference contract's depositsCount remains 1 (unchanged), while the buggy contract's depositsCount also remains 1 (no difference there). Actually, the correct divergence is that after owner sends money to the target (non-owner), in reference, the target receives ether; in buggy, the owner is not allowed so the call reverts. Let me pick: after a non-owner deposits, the owner calls sendMoney on a non-owner address; reference succeeds and target gets ether (balance of target increases), bug reverts (target balance unchanged).
change_summary: Change modifier condition from msg.sender == owner to msg.sender != owner
